title: Presale Marketing: You Don't Need Better Renderings, You Need More Detail
seoTitle: Presale Marketing: More Detail, Not Better Renderings
description: Beautiful brochures and renderings are not enough to sell presale units. Buyers need granular information about their own unit, room by room.
answer: Most presale projects already have beautiful renderings, brochures and videos. What is missing is granularity: information about each buyer's own unit, room by room, that a normal buyer can understand without reading a floorplan.
body:
When a developer tells me sales are slow, the first instinct is to ask for better visuals. In most cases, that is the wrong fix.

## The marketing package is usually fine

Most projects I see already have a beautiful brochure, well-made renderings, polished videos and great amenity images. Quality is not the problem.

## The problem is granularity

All of that material talks about the building. The buyer is trying to understand **their** unit. And at that level, the information is thin and uncertain.

## Floorplans are easy for us, not for buyers

For people in the industry, reading a floorplan is a piece of cake. For a normal buyer, it is not. They can look at it, they can get a rough idea, but then the real questions arrive:

- If I put a king bed here, can I still walk around it?
- Is there space for a chair, or an ottoman?
- How big does the bathroom actually feel?

When they cannot answer those questions, they hesitate. Hesitation is what slows a presale down.

## Go down to every room

The goal is not more detail in general. It is information at the right level: not just the building, not just the unit, but every room inside every unit. The buyer should be able to understand, safely and on their own, what they are buying.

So no, most projects do not need better visualization. They need more granular visualization.
takeaways: Quality of renderings is rarely what slows a presale down.
Marketing materials describe the building; buyers want to understand their unit.
Most buyers cannot read a floorplan well enough to feel sure.
Information about every room in every unit is what removes hesitation.
faq: What does granular visualization mean in real estate?
Visual information at the level of each unit and each room, so a buyer can see their own space instead of a typical or hero unit.
Why are floorplans not enough for buyers?
Floorplans are abstract. Most buyers cannot judge from them how big a room feels or whether their furniture will fit, so doubts remain.
Do better renderings increase presale sales?
They help the overall image of the project, but they do not answer the buyer's question about their own unit, which is usually what blocks the decision.
